page: Microsoft Azure D96as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine within the DASv5 series, deployed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor operating at 3.525 GHz, supplying 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading enabled. Memory provisioning stands at 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark assessments confirm exceptional parallel compute throughput, with multi-core stress-ng scoring 129,535.28 and PassMark CPU encryption exceeding 102,623, both placing in the top ten percent of cloud environments. Synthetic compiling performance via Clang (52,486.0) and ray tracing (88,233.0) place within the top quartile. In memory-intensive tracking, PassMark memory scored in the top tier at 3,165.1, while cached small-block read bandwidth reached 6,004.39 GB/sec. Uncached large-block reads and writes operate closer to industry averages at 126.88 GB/sec and 66.80 GB/sec, matching typical Zen 3 memory interconnect constraints.

The instance does not bundle local NVMe or ephemeral storage, requiring attached remote managed disks such as Azure Premium Storage for all persistent and scratch filesystem requirements. Similarly, the server provides no hardware accelerators (zero GPUs) or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, focusing all capacity strictly on dense x86 CPU and memory computation. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high ratio of 96 dedicated vCPUs to 384 GB RAM offers strong economy for compute-dense parallel workloads without paying the premium associated with specialized memory-heavy or GPU hardware classes.

With strong results in database operations (27,134.4 on PassMark) and high-throughput key-value operations (89.83 million Redis SET operations per second), the D96as_v5 is well matched for horizontally and vertically scaled backend applications. Key target workloads include enterprise web application serving, continuous integration and parallel build pipelines, batch data processing, distributed caching layers, and multi-threaded enterprise database backends.
description: Microsoft Azure D96as_v5 is a general-purpose server powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores at 3.525 GHz, accompanied by 384.0 GB of RAM. The instance features a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, offering hardware support for AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. Benchmark results place its multi-core compute in the top tier, demonstrating 129,535.28 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 89.83 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance includes no bundled local storage or GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached remote storage. Lacking hardware accelerators, it offers an economical, resource-dense platform for parallel processing without memory-optimized or accelerator premiums. The D96as_v5 is well suited for enterprise application servers, large compilation suites, distributed caching, and multi-threaded relational or in-memory databases.
